benchmark_location: Casa Batlló, Passeig de Gràcia 43, Barcelona
benchmark_description: 6-class urban perception audit: OCR, traffic control, street furniture, vehicles, road markings, infrastructure keypoints. Each VLM loaded sequentially on NVIDIA L4 (24 GB), bfloat16, flash-attn 2.

InternVL2.5 8B.pros: Best keypoint precision (80.7 px); best composite score; strong schema compliance
InternVL2.5 8B.cons: 0 IoU across all detection categories like all models — 7B VLMs lack spatial coordinate regression for pixel-accurate boxes

Qwen 2.5 VL 7B.pros: Second-best composite; good JSON structure; native Flash Attention 2 support; best OSS ecosystem (HuggingFace, vLLM, Ollama)
Qwen 2.5 VL 7B.cons: Keypoint distance 4x worse than InternVL2; 0 IoU on detections

Idefics3 8B.cons: Requires Meta Llama 3 license gate; poor spatial precision; lower composite score

Phi-3.5 Vision.pros: Smallest footprint (4.2B); fast inference on L4
Phi-3.5 Vision.cons: Outputs float coords (0-1) instead of int (0-1000) — schema fails for real images; lowest composite

LLaVA-OneVision 7B.pros: Strong spatial grounding in research papers; good JSON compliance
LLaVA-OneVision 7B.cons: Worst keypoint distance by far (6087 px == essentially random); poor object localization
